book: Gurbani — Selections from the Guru Granth Sahib

1: [Guru Granth Sahib — The great shabad of Guru Nanak]

There is no Hindu, there is no Muslim — so whose path shall I follow? I shall follow God's path. God is neither Hindu nor Muslim, and the body of God is neither. If God is in the mosque, then who is in the wilderness? He who made the clay of both is not in either — and the quarrel of the two is a quarrel over a coat, while the wearer goes unclothed.

Nanak says: Three things are difficult in this age of darkness — to give without being asked, to remember the Name in the midst of the world, and to eat the bread of honest labour. He who does these three carries a lamp through the dark age, and the lamp is enough, for the dark age is not dark to the lamp.
2: [Guru Angad — The body and the temple]

The body is the temple of the Lord, and the Lord's light is in it. Why do you seek Him in stone and in water, when the search is in the chest? Open the door of the chest with the key of the Guru's word, and the temple you were looking for is the one you are standing in.

He alone serves who has love in his heart. The rest serve for wages, and the wage of serving for wages is wages — but the wage of love is the Beloved, and the Beloved is not a wage but a home. Serve with love, and the serving is the reward, and the reward never ends.
3: [Guru Arjan — The garden of the world]

The world is a garden planted by the One Gardener, and every creature in it is His plant. Some are watered and some are waiting, and the waiting is not neglect — the Gardener knows the season of each plant, and the frost that kills one is the water of another, and He has not made one mistake in the planting.
[Guru Tegh Bahadur — The hymn of the nine treasures]

Says Nanak: the mouth that does not remember the Name has wasted its speech, and the ears that do not hear His praise have wasted their hearing, and the eyes that do not see Him in every face have wasted their seeing. Wake, O my soul — the nine treasures of the world are under the threshold of the Name, and the threshold is not far: it is under your own feet, and you have been standing on it your whole life.
